request.spec:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Sign-in and sheet loading are in, and `bin/e2e` passes (1 test passed).

**How it works:**
- **Sign-in:** at `/` you type a name (`signin-name`) and press `signin-submit`; there's no password. The name then shows in `current-user`. A blank name shows `signin-error`. The name only lives in the page: it isn't saved on the server, but every request sends it in an `X-User` header.
- **Sheets:** once signed in, you type an id (`sheet-id-input`) and press `sheet-load`. The server returns that sheet, creating it if it has never been used, and the id shows in `sheet-current-id`. A refused load shows `sheet-load-error`, which clears when you edit the field or try again. Signing in as another name clears the active sheet.
- **Stored data:** a new database migration (`V1__sheet.sql`) adds a `sheet` table holding the id, who created it and when. Later per-sheet data can hang off it.

**Server:** a new `sheet` package with the entity, repository, service and controller, plus one endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{id}/load`. The id and user name must be non-blank and at most 100 characters. If two users load the same new sheet at once, both get the same sheet.

**Front end:**
- `core/session.ts` holds the signed-in name and the active sheet.
- `core/session-bar.ts` is the sign-in and sheet bar, added to the app shell.
- The home page now shows its content only once a sheet is loaded.

Two things to know:
- **Throwaway sheets:** the test helper's re-load step loads an extra `<id>-reload` sheet, so each re-load leaves an empty sheet row in the database.
- **Angular version:** the project is on Angular 21.2, but `DESIGN.md` assumes v22. I used `@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })` because the `@Service` decorator it asks for doesn't exist in 21, and plain signal-bound inputs instead of Signal Forms.
